text: The agriculture, forestry and fishing sector employs 238,090 workers in England and Wales. This is 0.9% of the total workforce and the 16th-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 23.4% of workers in agriculture, forestry and fishing hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The agriculture sector is the least evenly spread of all sectors across England and Wales, with over half of all local authorities having a very low industry concentration ratio (under 0.6). In contrast, there are particularly high concentrations in some local authorities across Wales, the South West, and Yorkshire and The Humber. 

The agriculture sector shows a general trend where the higher the industry concentration ratio, the lower the proportion of workers with higher education qualifications tends to be. 

Manufacturing, construction, and wholesale and retail show the same trend. 

Powys (9.4%) and Eden (9.1%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the agriculture sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 0.9%.  

Of those working in the agriculture sector, 16.7% in Powys and 17.0% in Eden have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 7.3 and 7.0 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 24.0%. 

Barking and Dagenham, and Merton (both 0.04%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the agriculture sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 0.9%.  

Of those working in agriculture, 42.9% in Barking and Dagenham and 55.6% in Merton have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 18.9 percentage points and 31.6 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 24.0%. 

The occupations with the most workers in the agriculture sector are farmer (19.6%) and farm worker (13.6%). 

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the agriculture sector are chartered and certified accountants (92.7%) and business and related research professionals (80.0%).

text: The manufacturing sector employs 2.0 million workers in England and Wales. This is 7.4% of the total workforce and the fifth-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 32.4% of workers in manufacturing hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The manufacturing sector is underrepresented in London. Across the Midlands and the north of England, there is a higher-than-average industry concentration ratio. As industry concentration increases, we tend to see a lower proportion of those working in the sector having higher education qualifications. 

Barrow-in-Furness (17.9%) and North Lincolnshire (17.4%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in manufacturing, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 7.4%.  

Of those working in manufacturing, 34.1% in Barrow-in-Furness and 23.6% in North Lincolnshire have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 1.7 percentage points above and 8.8 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 32.4%. 

Wandsworth (2.6%) and Westminster (2.7%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in manufacturing, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 7.4%.  

Of those working in manufacturing, 76.1% in Wandsworth and 75.4% in Westminster have higher education qualifications, 43.7 and 43.0 percentage points respectively above the sector-wide proportion of 32.4%.  

Not all local authorities follow the manufacturing trend of the lower qualifications the more concentrated the sector is. Warwick for example shows the reverse and has a higher-than-average proportion of workers employed in manufacturing, yet 61.7% of these workers have a higher education qualification. Dudley and Wolverhampton have a similar manufacturing concentration ratio to Warwick but have higher education qualifications of 20.0% and 22.0% respectively. 

The difference in higher education qualifications is likely because of the type of occupations present in the manufacturing sector in Warwick. For example, 31.0% of those in Warwick's manufacturing sector work in professional occupations, and 15.0% work in associate professional occupations. Comparatively, 12.6% work in professional occupations and 11.8% in associate professional occupations nationally. 

Sectors displaying the same trend of higher-concentrated industries having lower-qualified workers include agriculture, forestry and fishing, construction, and wholesale and retail. 

Production managers and directors in manufacturing (8.8%), and food, drink and tobacco process operatives (5.0%) have the most workers. Managers are one of the most common occupations because senior positions in the manufacturing sector are grouped together, while junior roles are allocated to more specific occupations. 

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the manufacturing sector are natural and social science professionals (94.5%) and chartered and certified accountants (94.3%).

text: The electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply sector employs 161,700 workers in England and Wales. This is 0.6% of the total workforce and the 18th-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 45.9% of workers in electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The electricity sector is relatively evenly distributed in terms of concentration across England and Wales. However, there are a few local authorities where it is relatively concentrated. Lancaster has the greatest industry concentration ratio for the sector at 4.1, meaning it has four times the national average of workers employed in the electricity sector proportionally. 

The electricity sector does show a clear trend between concentration and higher education percentage, similar to the education, and human health and social care sectors. 

Lancaster (2.4%) and Hinckley and Bosworth (2.2%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the electricity sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 0.6%. 

Of those working in electricity, 55.0% in Lancaster and 31.7% in Hinckley and Bosworth have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 9.1 percentage points above and 14.2 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 45.9%. 

Cambridge and Craven are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the electricity sector, both with 0.2%, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 0.6%.  

Of those working in electricity, 77.4% in Cambridge and 50.0% in Craven have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 31.5 percentage points and 4.1 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 45.9%. 

The occupations with the most workers in the electricity sector are customer service occupations (6.4%), and plumbers and heating and ventilator installers and repairers (5.4%).  

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the electricity sector are chartered and certified accountants (94.4%) and chief executives and senior officials (87.8%).

text: The water supply, sewerage, waste management and remediation activities sector employs 203,785 workers in England and Wales. This is 0.7% of the total workforce and the 17th-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 28.4% of workers in the water supply and waste management sector hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The water supply and waste management sector is evenly distributed across England and Wales apart from a few pockets, most notably in south Wales and the North West.  

The sector does not show a clear trend when looking at higher education qualifications and industry concentration ratio. However, this is the only sector where workers living in London did not have a higher percentage of higher education qualifications. 

The education, and human health and social care sectors also do not show a clear trend. 

Copeland (19.1%) and Allerdale (6.8%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the water supply and waste management sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 0.7%.  

Of those working in water supply and waste management, 42.8% in Copeland and 50.4% in Allerdale have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 14.4 percentage points and 22.0 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 28.4%. 

Tower Hamlets and Camden are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the water supply and waste management sector, both with 0.1%, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 0.7%.  

Of those working in water supply and waste management, 39.5% in Tower Hamlets and 41.4% in Camden have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 11.1 percentage points and 13.0 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 28.4%. 

Copeland in the North West has the highest concentration of any sector, in any local authority, which is likely to be because of nuclear decommissioning in the area requiring a usually high volume of workers. The highly skilled nature of this work is shown by the much higher percentage (26.2%) of workers in Copeland in the sector in professional occupations. In comparison, the proportion of workers in professional occupations across the sector is 12.6%. 

The occupations with the most workers in the water supply and waste management sector are refuse and salvage occupations (11.2%) and large goods vehicle drivers (7.9%). 

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the water supply and waste management sector are chartered and certified accountants (92.8%) and environment professionals (76.0%).

text: The construction sector employs 2.4 million workers in England and Wales. This is 8.7% of the total workforce and the fourth-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 24.5% of workers in construction hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
In the construction sector, as industry concentration within a particular local authority increases, we tend to see a lower proportion of those working in the sector having higher education qualifications. Manufacturing, agriculture, forestry and fishing, and wholesale and retail all follow a similar pattern to construction. 

The construction sector is evenly distributed across England and Wales, but local authorities in London have a generally lower industry concentration. 

Castle Point (14.5%) and Maldon (14.4%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the construction sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 8.7%. 

Of those working in construction, 15.2% in Castle Point and 17.2% in Maldon have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 9.3 and 7.3 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 24.5%. 

Tower Hamlets (3.2%) and Kensington and Chelsea (3.3%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the construction sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 8.7%. 

Of those working in construction, 45.4% in Tower Hamlets and 53.5% in Kensington and Chelsea have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 20.9 and 29.0 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 24.5%. 

There are 12.8% of workers in the construction sector who have apprenticeships as their highest qualification. This is the highest of all industry sectors and more than twice the average for England and Wales across all industries (5.0%). South Lakeland (19.0%), Scarborough (18.5%) and Swansea (18.0%) are the local authorities where the highest proportion of workers in construction came through apprenticeships. 

In construction, almost half of workers are in skilled trades occupations. Production managers and directors in construction (11.1%) and construction and building trades (8.3%) had the most workers.  

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the construction sector are quantity surveyors (80.4%) and engineering professionals (77.5%).

text: The wholesale and retail trade; repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles sector employs 4.2 million workers in England and Wales. This is 15.0% of the total workforce and the highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 26.7% of workers in wholesale hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
In the wholesale sector, as industry concentration within a particular local authority increases, we tend to see a lower proportion of those working in the sector having higher education qualifications. Manufacturing, construction, and agriculture, forestry and fishing all follow a similar pattern to wholesale. 

The sector tends to be more highly concentrated outside London. 

Tamworth (21.4%) and Doncaster (21.1%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the wholesale sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 15.0%. 

Of those working in wholesale, 18.4% in Tamworth and 18.7% in Doncaster have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 8.3 and 8.0 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 26.7%.  

Cambridge and Oxford are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the wholesale sector. Only 8.6% of workers in Cambridge and 9.3% of workers in Oxford work in wholesale, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 15.0%. 

Of those working in wholesale, 38.9% in Cambridge and 31.1% in Oxford have higher education qualifications. These are 12.2 and 4.4 percentage points respectively above the sector-wide proportion of 26.7%. 

Local authorities in London tend to have a higher proportion of workers in wholesale with higher education qualifications than elsewhere in England and Wales. For example, Kingston upon Thames and Cardiff have approximately the same industry concentration (0.8). However, Kingston upon Thames has 43.6% of workers in wholesale with higher education qualifications, while for Cardiff, this is 29.9%. 

The occupations with the most workers in the wholesale sector are sales and retail assistants (23.9%) and managers and directors in retail and wholesale (10.3%). Managers are one of the most common occupations because senior positions in the wholesale sector are grouped together, while junior roles are allocated to more specific occupations. 

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the wholesale sector are optometrists (95.6%) and chartered and certified accountants (92.8%).

text: The transport and storage sector employs 1.4 million workers in England and Wales. This is 5.0% of the total workforce and the ninth-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 23.5% of workers in transport and storage hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The transport and storage sector is relatively evenly distributed across England and Wales, with a few pockets of higher concentration, mainly in the Midlands.  

As industry concentration increases, we tend to see a lower proportion of those working in the sector having higher education qualifications. This is similar to the manufacturing and agriculture sectors. 

Crawley (12.9%) and Slough (12.2%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the transport and storage sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 5.0%. 

Of those working in transport and storage, 25.7% in Crawley and 29.8% in Slough have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 2.2 percentage points below and 6.3 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 23.5%. 

Cambridge (2.3%) and Cheltenham (2.5%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the transport and storage sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 5.0%.  

Of those working in transport and storage, 28.7% in Cambridge and 28.4% in Cheltenham have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 5.2 and 4.9 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 23.5%. 

Four of the five local authorities with the highest concentration of transport and storage are just outside London and close to the M25, the exception, Luton, is near the M1, a major transport route to London. 

The occupations with the most workers in the transport and storage sector are taxi and cab drivers and chauffeurs (9.2%) and large goods vehicle drivers (8.4%).  

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the transport and storage sector are programmers and software development professionals (72.4%) and aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers (69.4%).

text: The accommodation and food service activities sector employs 1.4 million workers in England and Wales. This is 4.9% of the total workforce and the 10th-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 25.1% of workers in the accommodation sector hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The local authorities in which the accommodation sector is highly concentrated are in areas that traditionally see a high volume of tourism, for example, London, Cornwall, the Lake District, west Wales and north Wales.  

We see a general trend in the accommodation sector that the higher the industry concentration ratio, the lower qualification levels tend to be. 

Manufacturing, construction, and agriculture, forestry and fishing show the same trend. 

Local authorities that are home to seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Great Yarmouth still have greater accommodation sector concentration than most local authorities, but the proportion of their workers with higher education qualifications are significantly lower than comparable local authorities. For example, Great Yarmouth has an industry concentration of 1.7 and 13.5% of those workers in the sector have higher education qualifications, this is the lowest of all local authorities. Compare this with Newham in London, which has a similar industry concentration, but 32.1% of its workers in accommodation have higher education qualifications.  

South Lakeland (11.6%) and Scarborough (10.6%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the accommodation sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 4.9%.  

Of those working in accommodation, 29.2% in South Lakeland and 21.7% in Scarborough have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 4.1 percentage points above and 3.4 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 25.1%. 

Wokingham (2.9%) and Rochford (3.1%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the accommodation sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 4.9%.  

Of those working in accommodation, 30.1% in Wokingham and 13.7% in Rochford have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 5.0 percentage points above and 11.4 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 25.1%. 

The occupations with the most workers in the accommodation sector are kitchen and catering assistants (14.2%) and chefs (12.4%). 

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the accommodation sector are financial managers and directors (70.1%) and human resource managers and directors (57.3%).

text: The information and communication sector employs 1.3 million workers in England and Wales. This is 4.6% of the total workforce and the 11th-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 64.8% of workers in information and communication hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
For the information and communication sector, the higher the industry concentration, the greater proportion of workers with higher education qualifications. The sector is highly concentrated in London and the South East. 

Professional, scientific and technical activities, and finance and insurance services show the same trend. 

Wokingham (15.0%) and Reading (12.1%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the information and communication sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 4.6%.  

Of those working in the information and communication sector, 72.2% in Wokingham and 76.5% in Reading have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 7.4 percentage points and 11.7 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 64.8%. 

Boston (0.9%) and North East Lincolnshire (1.3%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the information and communication sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 4.6%.  

Of those working in the information and communication sector, 41.3% in Boston and 40.1% in North East Lincolnshire have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 23.5 percentage points and 24.7 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 64.8%. 

Cardiff's industry concentration has a slightly higher proportion of its workers having higher education qualifications, 70.9% in comparison with 64.8%. Monmouthshire (64.9%) and the Vale of Glamorgan (61.7%) have the next two highest industry concentrations in Wales. This may be because of Cardiff being the media centre for Wales, the national broadcaster has their headquarters in the city centre and the third-largest media cluster in the UK. 

The occupations with the most workers in the information and communication sector are programmers and software development professionals (11.0%) and information technology directors (6.5%).  

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the information and communication sector are chartered and certified accountants (95.3%) and actuaries, economists and statisticians (93.7%).

text: The finance and insurance activities sector employs 1.0 million workers in England and Wales. This is 3.8% of the total workforce and the 12th-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 56.8% of workers in the finance and insurance sector hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The finance and insurance sector is concentrated largely in London, the South East and East of England. There is a general trend where the higher the industry concentration the higher the proportion of workers in finance and insurance who have higher education qualifications. 

Professional, scientific and technical activities, and information and communication show the same trend. 

Kensington and Chelsea (15.5%) and Westminster (13.8%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the finance and insurance sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 3.8%.  

Of those working in finance and insurance, 87.1% in Kensington and Chelsea, and 88.5% in Westminster have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 30.3 percentage points and 31.7 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 56.8%. 

Copeland (0.6%) and East Lindsey (0.8%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the finance and insurance sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 3.8%.  

Of those working in finance and insurance, 38.5% in Copeland and 35.2% in East Lindsey have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 18.3 percentage points and 21.6 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 56.8%. 

The occupations with the most workers in the finance and insurance sector are financial managers and directors (13.5%) and finance and investment analysts and advisors (11.4%). Managers are one of the most common occupations because senior positions in the finance and insurance sector are grouped together, while junior roles are allocated to more specific occupations.  

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the finance and insurance sector are solicitors and lawyers (97.1%) and actuaries, economists and statisticians (95.7%).

text: The real estate activities sector employs 430,775 workers in England and Wales. This is 1.6% of the total workforce and the 15th-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 44.9% of workers in real estate activities hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The real estate sector is more concentrated around London and the South East than the rest of England and Wales.  

There is not a clear association between higher industry concentration ratio and the level of highest qualifications in the real estate sector. However, local authorities with a high concentration of the real estate sector are very slightly more likely to have higher proportions of workers with higher education. This trend is substantially weaker than in other sectors with highly qualified workforces. 

Kensington and Chelsea (3.6%) and Hertsmere (3.3%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in real estate, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 1.6%.  

Of those working in real estate, 65.2% in Kensington and Chelsea, and 40.8% in Hertsmere have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 20.3 percentage points above and 4.1 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 44.9%.  

Barrow-in-Furness (0.6%) and Copeland (0.7%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in real estate, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 1.6%.  

Of those working in real estate, 34.2% in Barrow-in-Furness and 38.6% in Copeland have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 10.7 percentage points and 6.3 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 44.9%. 

The occupations with the most workers in the real estate sector are property, housing and estate managers (28.7%) and estate agents and auctioneers (9.4%).  

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the real estate sector are chartered and certified accountants (94.1%) and solicitors and lawyers (93.1%).

text: The professional, scientific and technical activities sector employs 1.8 million workers in England and Wales. This is 6.6% of the total workforce and the sixth-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 70.2% of workers in professional, scientific and technical activities hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The professional and scientific sector is highly concentrated in London and the South East, although there are some pockets of higher concentrations in the Midlands and across the north of England. 

For the professional and scientific sector, the higher the industry concentration, the greater proportion of workers with higher education qualifications. Information and communication, arts and recreation, and financial and insurance services display the same trend. 

Islington (17.3%) and Camden (16.1%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the professional and scientific sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 6.6%.  

Of those working in professional and scientific sector, 89.3% in Islington and 88.7% in Camden have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 19.1 and 18.5 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 70.2%.  

Blaenau Gwent (2.3%) and Boston (2.4%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the professional and scientific sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 6.6%. 

Of those working in the professional and scientific sector, 57.6% in Blaenau Gwent and 42.8% in Boston have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 12.6 and 27.4 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 70.2%. 

Harrogate has highest concentration of workers in the professional and scientific sector in Yorkshire and The Humber, employing 9.0% of workers in the local authority. This is partly because of the presence of a large pharmaceutical development, crop production and chemical development facility. The advanced qualifications required for this type of work probably also explains why professional and scientific sector workers in Harrogate have the highest percentage of higher education qualifications in this sector in Yorkshire and The Humber.

The occupations with the most workers in the professional and scientific sector are solicitors and lawyers (6.3%) and book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks (4.4%).   

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the professional and scientific sector are barristers and judges (97.8%) and solicitors and lawyers (97.5%).

text: The administrative and support service activities sector employs 1.45 million workers in England and Wales. This is 5.2% of the total workforce and the eighth-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 27.6% of workers in administrative and support, hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The administrative and support sector is relatively evenly distributed across England and Wales. Although Welsh local authorities do tend to have a slightly lower concentration and those in London and the South East tend to be slightly higher. 

The administrative and support sector does not show a clear trend when it comes to the concentration of an industry and the proportion of workers who have higher education qualifications. This is similar to the human health and social work activities, and education sectors. 

Newham (8.6%) and Boston (8.3%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the administrative and support sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 5.2%. 

Of those working in administrative and support, 32.3% in Newham and 13.0% in Boston have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 4.7 percentage points above and 14.6 percentage points below the sector average of 27.6%.  

Carmarthenshire (3.5%) and Cambridge (3.8%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in the administrative and support sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 5.2%. 

Of those working in administrative and support, 23.9% in Carmarthenshire and 36.0% in Cambridge have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 3.7 percentage points below and 8.4 percentage points above the sector average of 27.6%. 

In the administrative and support sector, workers in London have consistently higher percentages of higher education qualifications (37.5%) than in other regions, with the next highest being the South East (27.7%).  

The occupations with the most workers in the administrative and support sector are cleaners and domestics (21.2%) and gardeners and landscape gardeners (7.3%).   

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the administrative and support sector are chartered and certified accountants (90.2%) and other nursing professionals (83.5%).

text: The public administration and defence; compulsory social security sector employs 1.6 million workers in England and Wales. This is 5.9% of the total workforce and the seventh-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 50.0% of workers in public administration hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The public administration sector is relatively evenly spread across much of England and Wales, apart from local authorities in London where concentrations tend to be lower, and in south Wales where concentrations tend to be higher. 

The public administration sector shows a trend where the higher the concentration ratio usually the lower the proportion of workers with higher education qualifications, it is the only sector with a more highly qualified workforce to follow this trend. Manufacturing, construction, and agriculture, forestry and fishing follow this same pattern. 

Richmondshire (20.8%) and North Kesteven (14.3%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in public administration, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 5.9%.  

Of those working in public administration, 32.2% in Richmondshire and 44.9% in North Kesteven have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 17.8 and 5.1 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 50.0%. 

Kensington and Chelsea (2.4%) and Cambridge (2.8%) are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers in public administration, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 5.9%.  

Of those working in public administration, 75.9% in Kensington and Chelsea, and 73.4% in Cambridge have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 25.9 and 23.4 percentage points above the industry average of 50.0%. 

Cheltenham shows a higher education qualification level of 73.1%, which is higher than expected given the public administration and defence industry concentration ratio of 1.49. Local authorities with similar industry concentration ratios such as Portsmouth and West Suffolk have higher education qualification levels of 49.5% and 34.1% respectively. This could be because of a large government department in the area that likely employs occupations in the professional category.  

The occupations with the most workers in the public administration sector are national government administrative occupations (9.6%) and police officers (sergeants and below) (8.4%). 

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the public administration sector are solicitors and lawyers (97.7%) and judges and barristers (94.6%).

text: The education sector employs 2.7 million workers in England and Wales. This is 9.8% of the total workforce and the third-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 64.9% of workers in education hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The education sector is relatively evenly distributed across England and Wales. In the sector, 70.2% of local authorities have a moderate concentration meaning that the proportion of workers in those local authorities is similar to the proportion in England and Wales as a whole. 

The education sector does not show a clear trend when it comes to the concentration of an industry and the proportion of workers who have higher education qualifications. This is similar to the human health and social work activities, and administrative and support services sectors. 

Richmond upon Thames (11.8%) and Cambridge (21.5%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the education sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 9.8%.  

Of those working in education, 79.7% in Richmond upon Thames and 79.3% in Cambridge have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 14.8 percentage points and 14.4 percentage points above the sector-wide proportion of 64.9%. 

Crawley and Boston are the two local authorities employing the lowest percentage of workers (both 6.3%) in the education sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 9.8%.  

Of those working in education, 50.1% in Crawley and 50.5% in Boston have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 14.8 and 14.4 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 64.9%. 

Cambridge and Oxford are the only two local authorities where the industry concentration ratio exceeds 2, at 2.2 and 2.4 respectively. This is likely because of their universities, which are recognised and respected institutions across the world, hiring numerous researchers and professionals, and attracting scholars and academics.  

Other areas follow this pattern where local authorities with large universities compared with their population size have higher industry concentration and education levels. Ceredigion and Canterbury both have an education industry concentration greater than average (1.3 and 1.6 respectively) and higher education levels than the sector-wide proportion of 64.9%, at 71.5% and 70.5% respectively. This is likely because of the presence of Aberystwyth University and University of Kent in these areas. 

The occupations with the most workers in the education sector are secondary education teaching professionals (11.0%) and primary education teaching professionals (10.6%)  

The occupations with the highest proportion of workers with higher education qualifications in the education sector are headteachers and principals (96.9%) and higher education teaching professionals (96.7%).

text: The human health and social work activities sector employs 4.1 million workers in England and Wales. This is 14.7% of the total workforce and the second-highest of all industrial sectors. Across England and Wales, 53.2% of workers in health hold higher education qualifications.
textlater:
The health sector is generally more concentrated away from London. Several local authorities with a higher-than-average industry concentration are located near the coastline, as well as substantial clusters in the North West, Wales and the South West. 

Sectors such as health that do not show a clear trend when it comes to the local authority concentration of an industry and the proportion of workers who have higher education qualifications include education, and administrative and support services. 

Eastbourne (21.8%) and Denbighshire (21.2%) are the two local authorities employing the highest percentage of workers in the health sector, compared with the sector-wide proportion of 14.7%.  

Of those working in health, 48.4% in Eastbourne and 49.9% in Denbighshire have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 4.8 percentage points and 3.3 percentage points below the sector-wide proportion of 53.2%.
